provenance: ADR-032 §g, the legacy-HTML image case and the ONLY one of the three goldens whose containing-item labels discriminate. Bank of America FY2006 10-K, evals/fixtures/bac-2006 (provenance in evals/fixtures/README.md), 4,517,513 raw bytes, 705,848 normalized chars, doc_status `success` with zero warnings. Five tags, raw byte offsets 1595161, 1597827, 2719349, 2719544 and 2727411, all uppercase-tagged 1990s-style markup: ``, unquoted-lowercase nowhere, no style attribute on any of them and therefore `width`/`height` null on all five -- which is the point of choosing this fixture over a modern one: it pins that a MISSING declared size is reported as null and not invented, and that html.parser's attribute-name lowercasing is what makes SRC/ALT readable at all. All five carry the same useless alt text, "LOGO", which is also worth pinning: the annotation reports what the filer wrote, it does not improve it. WHY THIS FIXTURE CARRIES THE ITEM LABELS. bac-2006 is the only one of the three whose segmentation is clean -- `success`, no warnings, no dominance -- so its images fall in two DIFFERENT items: the two trading-VaR charts in Item 7 (MD&A) at 289566 and 291296, and the signature/auditor-report images in Item 8 at 391006 (twice) and 396493. On xom-2021 and jpm-2024 every image lands in one dominated span, so those cases cannot tell a working containment derivation from a constant; this one can. A regression that computed containment off the wrong end of a span, or off the item list order, is red here. The two images at 391006 share an offset: they are adjacent tags with only markup between them, so both sit at the same point in normalized_text. That is correct and deliberate -- an emits no text, so two adjacent ones are at the same place -- and the case pins it so a future implementation cannot 'fix' it by nudging offsets apart. `images_sane` is min=max=5, an EXACT count rather than the band ADR-029's table cases use, because no image is ever dropped (unlike an all-empty spacer table): the record count is the raw count, full stop, so a drop rule sneaking in is red. HOW THE LABELS WERE MADE (ADR-032 §g). `src`, `alt`, `width` and `height` are read off the RAW HTML: every tag matched with a plain attribute regex, entity-decoded, the pixel size taken from the width=/height= attribute if there is one and otherwise from the `style` declaration (0 of the corpus's 53 carry the attribute form, 40 carry the style form -- ADR-032 §b1). That read is an INDEPENDENT second route, written for the purpose and not sharing a line with src/sec10k/normalize.py's recorder, and it is compared field by field against the shipped annotation before any label is written; a disagreement aborts the authoring script rather than being written down. `offset` is the annotation's own; it is not blindly copied, because `before` and `after` are the 30 characters of normalized_text on either side of it and those ARE hand-checkable against the raw file -- an offset that drifted by even one character would leave `before`/`after` no longer matching what the raw HTML has around the tag. `item` is derived the way ADR-029 derives an item's tables, from offsets alone (the item whose [start, end) span holds the offset, null when no span does), never from a stored field.
